one: Modern applied statistical learning: prediction methods, model evaluation, optimization, and generative models.
pos: STATS 315A is a graduate-level ML course in the statistics department, covering prediction methods (linear models, trees/forests, deep networks), model evaluation (cross-validation, calibration, conformal prediction), optimization (convexity, stochastic methods), and generative models (language models, diffusion, VAEs). It balances statistical rigor with modern methods.
prereq: Probability/statistics, linear algebra, ML basics (STATS 202/CS 229 level).
assess: Assignments plus a project/exam. Check the current syllabus for details.
who: Statistics/ML graduate students; people who want rigorous predictive modeling and uncertainty quantification.
tips: Take STATS 202 or CS 229 first. The conformal prediction part is worth going deep on.
